report.summary: Read fanout.py chunk 1 of 2; enumerated claims and observations.
risks: fan_out signature (line ~155) | medium | The signature includes graph_hops and brief_budget_chars but the chunk ends before the body; cannot verify that graph_hops is used or brief_budget_chars is enforced. | Check the rest of fan_out in chunk 2.

FanoutTask.key (line ~75) | low | The sanitization collapses dot runs after replacing separators; the comment claims traversal impossible, but the logic order is: replace separators with '_', then collapse '..'. This does prevent '..' but the claim about 'reads as though it were trying to' is subjective. | Verify with a test using '../../etc/passwd'.

_one_call (line ~100) | medium | The flight recorder records objective_sha256 and brief_chars but not the actual brief content; the claim 'did these three votes see the same prompt' is only partially answered because the brief is not hashed. | Check if brief is hashed elsewhere in the result.

DeepSeekProvider import (line ~96) | low | The comment says importing inside _one_call avoids pulling the provider stack for tooling that reads dataclasses, but fan_out also imports DeepSeekProvider indirectly? Actually _one_call is the only place; but fan_out may call _one_call, so the import happens at runtime. The claim is plausible but unverified. | Check if any module-level import of DeepSeekProvider exists elsewhere.

Default temperature 0.0 (line ~100) | medium | The docstring says votes need temperature > 0 and fan_out refuses the combination, but the default temperature parameter in _one_call is 0.0. The refusal must be in fan_out's body (chunk 2). | Check fan_out body for temperature enforcement.

handoff.purpose: Read the first half of fanout.py: module docstring, constants, dataclasses, and the _one_call helper.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY
symbols.note: Concurrency ceiling set to 8, with a measured rationale about a 900s timeout on 100 concurrent agents.

symbols.name: default_concurrency
symbols.note: Reads DAEDALUS_FANOUT_CONCURRENCY env var, clamps to at least 1, falls back to DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY on parse errors.

symbols.name: FanoutTask
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with task_id, objective, paths, votes, meta; key property derives a filename-safe identity.

symbols.name: FanoutResult
symbols.note: Mutable dataclass with task_id, key, votes_requested, answers, errors, meta, resumed, trace_id; ok property and to_dict method.

symbols.name: _one_call
symbols.note: Performs one advisory call to DeepSeekProvider, builds a flight-recorder dict with digests and metadata.

symbols.name: fan_out
symbols.note: Signature only in this chunk; body is in chunk 2. Takes tasks, out_dir, concurrency, model, timeout, graph_hops, brief_budget_chars, and a policy parameter.

claims.text: The guard is not optional here and not a parameter -- a fan-out is exactly the shape that turns a missing guard into a bill.
claims.why: The chunk does not show any call to install_process_guard; it is imported but not invoked in this window. The claim refers to behavior outside this chunk.

claims.text: votes is a first-class argument and every result records how many independent answers it is made of.
claims.why: FanoutTask has a votes field (line ~50) and FanoutResult has votes_requested and to_dict includes votes_collected (lines ~90-95).

claims.text: fan_out now REFUSES the combination [votes > 1 with temperature 0.0].
claims.why: The fan_out body is not in this chunk; the refusal must occur there. The signature shows no temperature parameter, so it must be derived from elsewhere or enforced in the body.

claims.text: A FRESH PROVIDER PER CALL. DeepSeekProvider.run resets self._written per call precisely so one instance cannot report a prior call's writes as this one's. Sharing an instance across worker threads would reintroduce that race by another door, so each call gets its own.
claims.why: In _one_call (line ~100) a new DeepSeekProvider() is constructed for each call, with a comment 'fresh per call -- see module docstring'.

claims.text: THE GRAPH GOES IN THE PROMPT. ... Tasks that name paths get render_brief prepended.
claims.why: This chunk imports render_brief and _one_call prepends a brief if present, but the logic that decides whether to call render_brief and how graph_hops/brief_budget_chars are used is in fan_out's body (chunk 2).

claims.text: RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT WRITTEN. Via daedalus.atomic, so a reader tailing the output directory during a four-hour run never sees half a JSON document.
claims.why: write_text_atomic is imported, but the actual writing happens in fan_out's body (chunk 2). This chunk does not show the write call.

claims.text: Advisory only. There is no writable parameter and adding one would be a mistake.
claims.why: The chunk shows _one_call passes writable=False to provider.run (line ~125), and the fan_out signature (line ~155) has no writable parameter.

claims.text: Concurrency ceiling. ... MEASURED 2026-07-30: a hundred concurrent agents pushed the test suite past a 900 s timeout, and the gate read that timeout as failing tests. The suite is 4,146 tests and 765 s on this box when idle -- NOT the 105 s the handoff carried.
claims.why: The measurement figures are external facts not verifiable from code in this chunk. The constant is set to 8, which is consistent with the claim but the numbers themselves are uncheckable.

claims.text: key is the filename the answer lands under and the resume identity, so it must be stable across runs and safe as a path segment. It is derived from task_id rather than trusted, because a task id built from a commit message or a file path will contain separators.
claims.why: The key property (lines ~65-80) sanitizes task_id by replacing non-alphanumeric/-_./ characters with '_', collapses '..', strips leading . and _, truncates to 80 chars, and appends a SHA-256 digest.

claims.text: The digest is appended rather than the sanitised name being trusted: a/b and a\b both sanitise to a_b, and two tasks sharing a result file would have one silently overwrite the other's answer.
claims.why: The key property appends a 10-char SHA-256 digest of the original task_id, so different task_ids that sanitize to the same name get different digests.

claims.text: Dot runs are collapsed after sanitising. Replacing separators already makes traversal impossible, but ../../etc/passwd still produced .._.._etc_passwd -- a key that cannot escape and reads as though it were trying to.
claims.why: The key property first replaces separators (and other chars) with '_', then collapses any '..' into '_'. For '../../etc/passwd', after sanitization: '.._.._etc_passwd' (since '/' becomes '_', so '..' remains until the while loop collapses them to '_'). The result cannot contain '..' and cannot escape.

claims.text: True when this result was loaded from disk rather than paid for again.
claims.why: The field exists, but the logic that sets it (loading from disk) is in fan_out's body (chunk 2).

claims.text: From daedalus.spine.envelope.current_trace_id, which NEVER mints -- so None means 'no trace was in scope', not 'here is a fresh unrelated id'.
claims.why: The chunk imports current_trace_id but does not show its implementation. The claim about its behavior is external.

claims.text: Present because the drift detector in tests/test_envelope_coverage.py caught this module as an undeclared record producer on 2026-07-30 and it was right: these files record a PAID external call and its answer, so a trace id correlates a bill to the run that incurred it.
claims.why: The test file is not in this chunk; the claim references external history.

claims.text: policy is handed to the provider, which passes it to daedalus.sensitivity.classify_data. Default None means the project's own policy applies -- so a caller that never heard of this argument gets the fence it already had, and widening egress is something an operator does on purpose at the call site rather than a default anybody inherits.
claims.why: The chunk shows policy is passed to provider.run (line ~122), but the provider's handling of policy is in another module.

claims.text: It cannot lift the secret floor. providers/deepseek.py calls secret_floor_rule per path independently of classify_data, and that rule is documented as running 'in EVERY lane, no bypass ... cannot be weakened by a project config'. Verified with a fully permissive policy: source files pass, .env is still refused.
claims.why: The provider implementation and secret_floor_rule are in other modules; this chunk only passes policy to the provider.

claims.text: Imported here, not at module scope: this module is imported by tooling that must not pull the provider stack (and its network config) just to read the dataclasses.
claims.why: The import of DeepSeekProvider is inside _one_call, not at module top level. The top-level imports do not include DeepSeekProvider.

claims.text: BEFORE the question, not after. A model that has already read the question treats the brief as supporting material; a model that reads the brief first treats the question as being about the thing described.
A fresh provider per call -- see module docstring
claims.why: A new DeepSeekProvider() is instantiated on each invocation of _one_call.

claims.text: temperature > 0 is what makes votes independent
claims.why: The temperature parameter is passed to provider.run, and the comment explicitly states that >0 makes votes independent. The default is 0.0, which is consistent with the need for enforcement elsewhere.

claims.text: writable=False, advisory only, structurally
claims.why: The provider.run call includes writable=False.

claims.text: THE FLIGHT RECORDER ... What was actually SENT, recorded next to what came back. ... DIGESTS, NOT BODIES, for the prompt: the objective carries whole file contents, and a recorder that copies them turns a 4 KB result file into a 60 KB one and duplicates the repo across runs/. The digest is what answers the questions that matter -- 'did these three votes see the same prompt', 'did the prompt change between runs', 'is this result stale' -- and those are identity questions, which is exactly what a hash is for. The system message IS kept whole: it is small, shared, and it was the thing nobody could see.
claims.why: The 'sent' dict includes objective_sha256, objective_chars, brief_chars, paths, model, temperature, system_override_sha256, system_override_chars, and policy. It does not include the full objective or brief, only digests and lengths. The system_override is kept whole via system_override_sha256? Actually it hashes it, so 'kept whole' is not accurate: it stores the hash, not the whole message. The comment says 'The system message IS kept whole', but the code stores a hash and length, not the message. However, the comment might refer to the fact that the system_override is included in the sent dict as a hash? Let's re-read: 'The system message IS kept whole' -- but the code hashes it. So this claim is BROKEN? The code stores system_override_sha256 and system_override_chars, not the full message. Therefore the claim 'kept whole' is not supported. However, the comment might mean that the system message is kept whole in the sense that it is not truncated? But the code only stores the hash. So verdict: BROKEN, line 137-139. Actually, the comment says 'The system message IS kept whole: it is small, shared, and it was the thing nobody could see.' But the code stores only a hash and length. So the claim is broken. Let's cite line 137-139.

claims.text: The system message IS kept whole: it is small, shared, and it was the thing nobody could see.
claims.why: The sent dict stores system_override_sha256 and system_override_chars, not the full message. So the system message is not kept whole; only its hash and length are recorded.

observations.what: The _one_call flight recorder hashes the objective and system_override, but does not hash the brief itself. The claim 'did these three votes see the same prompt' is only partially answered because the brief is not included in the digest.

The fan_out signature includes policy, graph_hops, and brief_budget_chars, but the chunk ends before the body. The enforcement of temperature > 0 for votes > 1 must be in the body, which is not visible here.
The comment about the system message being 'kept whole' contradicts the code that only stores a hash and length.
